verdict.rationale: Daytona documents programmatic sandbox creation and command execution through its SDKs (`sandbox = daytona.create()`, `sandbox.process.exec(...)` returning a response). It also ships an official MCP server so AI agents can interact with sandboxes programmatically, and CLI and SDK access to lifecycle management, which together cover the agent-driven end-to-end loop. missing for 10: an explicit documented delete/teardown API call (teardown rests only on 'shut them down just as fast' and generic lifecycle management), detail on reading execution output/exit codes, and independent hands-on corroboration of an agent running the full loop unattended.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, my agent can provision its own sandbox, execute code, read the results, and tear it down — end to end without a human

citations.quote: Daytona Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI agents to interact with Daytona Sandboxes programmatically.
Daytona provides methods to execute code in sandboxes.
Daytona provides command-line access to core features for interacting with Daytona Sandboxes, including managing their lifecycle, snapshots, and more.
Daytona lets you spin up sandboxes in milliseconds and shut them down just as fast.
An agent skill for creating and running sandboxes on the Daytona platform.
